text:
Sam (People Ops): quick Q from Kelly about 401(k) and taxes while on unpaid parental leave 1 - do contributions pause automatically? will there be tax or match implications?
Kelly: hi! i'll be taking 8 weeks unpaid leave and want to know if my pre-tax deferrals stop and whether employer match continues. also worried about hitting the annual contribution limit.
Iris (Finance): short answer: pre-tax deferrals stop if you're off payroll (no pay = nothing to defer). employer match is tied to actual payroll contributions, so match pauses when deferrals pause.
Kelly: bummer 1 can i make up missed deferrals later in the year or elect an after-tax catch-up?
Iris (Finance): you can increase your deferral percentage when you return, but we can't retroactively deduct pre-tax deferrals for pay you didn't receive. For people concerned about the annual limit, consider switching to post-tax (Roth) or increasing elective contributions after return, but consult tax advisor for personal guidance.
Sam (People Ops): notes for the leave packet: employees on unpaid leave should confirm with payroll whether deductions continue (e.g., medical, 401k loans). if deductions stop and you want to preserve vesting schedule or match, talk to manager and People Ops early; some customers opt to make lump-sum personal contributions outside payroll, but that doesn't affect employer match.
Payroll Bot: Reminder: To request voluntary after-tax contributions or change deferral % on return, submit the 401k change form at least 10 business days before the next payroll cycle: https://intranet.redwood/payroll/401k-change
Kelly: what about employer-paid benefits like the dependent-care stipend or 100% employer-paid life insurance during unpaid leave?
Iris (Finance): employer-paid benefits vary. Some stipends and employer-paid life insurance end when you're off payroll. We recommend reviewing the leave confirmation email People Ops sends; we also include a benefits impact summary. If you want an exception (e.g., continue stipend), manager + People Ops can submit an exception form to Payroll for review.
Kelly: ok thanks. one more: will missing a few pay periods affect RSU vesting?
Sam (People Ops): good question. vesting and equity are handled by the equity policy. short leaves under 90 days typically don't change the vesting schedule, but confirm with Compensation if leave is unpaid and exceeds policy windows. We'll add a line in the packet.
Iris (Finance): Pro tip: If you're worried about contribution limits or matching, schedule a 15-min with Payroll/Benefits before your leave. We can run scenarios on projected take-home and match impact.
Kelly: appreciate it 1 can People Ops add this to the leave checklist so future parents see it?
Sam (People Ops): will do. I'll paste the minimal checklist snippet here for the packet:
```
Payroll & Benefits - Unpaid Leave Checklist
- Confirm payroll enrollment status with People Ops before leave start.
- Will 401(k) deferrals continue? <yes/no> (Payroll note)
- Employer match during leave: <continues/pauses> (Finance confirm)
- Benefits affected (list): <medical, stipend, life insurance>
- RSU/equity vesting: <check with Compensation>
- Action items: schedule 1:1 with Payroll/Benefits; submit 401(k) change form if adjusting contributions on return.
```
Sam (People Ops): tagging @Iris can we add a short FAQ blurb to the leave packet about 401(k) match so employees see it upfront?
Iris (Finance): yes, i'll draft a 2-sentence blurb and send to People Ops by EOD. Also posting the payroll form link in the packet helps reduce follow-ups.
Payroll Bot: Form link: https://intranet.redwood/payroll/401k-change - Note: changes require 10 business days before payday.
Kelly: thank you all 1 i'll book the 15-min slot with payroll. :pray:
Sam (People Ops): thanks Kelly 1 will update the packet and confirm when the FAQ is live.
